title: Roman destruction of Jerusalem and the Second Temple, 70 CE
aliases: Siege and sack of Jerusalem, 70 CE
summary: During the First Jewish–Roman War, Roman forces under Titus besieged and captured Jerusalem in 70 CE. Near-contemporary testimony from Josephus describes the Temple being consumed by fire, while modern museum scholarship independently treats the siege, sack of the city, and destruction of the Temple as a major historical event. LEGEND owns the event historicity; it does not infer from the event alone that any scriptural prediction was supernaturally fulfilled.

time.note: LEGEND intentionally uses year-level precision for the canonical event. Ancient calendrical/day details in Josephus are source claims and need not be forced into one modern exact date here.

historicity.note: Confidence applies to the Roman siege/capture and destruction of the Second Temple in 70 CE, not to theological interpretations of the event.

counterpoints: The historical event and Mark 13:2 clearly concern destruction of the Jerusalem Temple, but that correspondence does not by itself establish supernatural prediction.
Scholarly dating of Mark is often placed around 65–75 CE, so the text's precise chronological relationship to the event should not be silently assumed.

uncertainty: Josephus is a near-contemporary participant/witness and major source, but his account still requires source criticism.
The exact sequence and responsibility for individual acts during the Temple fire is preserved as source-level detail rather than collapsed into a simplistic single-cause claim.
LEGEND does not decide the historical attribution, composition date, or theological fulfillment status of Mark 13:2.
alternative_interpretations: The Mark 13:2 narrative can be read as a pre-event prediction, a tradition shaped near the event, or a text finalized after the event depending on chronology and scholarly model.
Historical proof of the 70 CE destruction and textual proof that Mark 13:2 contains a prediction are independent propositions.

review.note: Canonical scope is the historical siege/capture and Second Temple destruction. Textual-prophecy fulfillment remains outside the event verdict.
